description: U.S. House districts for the 2028 election: 435 districts on the lines in effect for the November 3, 2026 election (the 2020-census apportionment; the 2030 census redraws every state for 2032). The per-district list is derived at generation time from data/presidential-results.json (The Downballot's district table, 2026 lines) and must total the seats below. Map status and redistricting risk are as of 2026-10-06.

riskLevels.stable: No live effort or litigation likely to change the 2028 lines.
riskLevels.low: An effort exists but is unlikely to produce a new map before 2028.
riskLevels.medium: Litigation or a legislative push could change the lines; outcome unclear.
riskLevels.high: A concrete mechanism aimed at 2028 is in motion (ballot question, announced redraw, court process).

AL.mapInUse2026: Legislature's June 2, 2026 map, after the Supreme Court lifted the Allen v. Milligan injunction (June 2, 2026) in the wake of Callais
AL.note: Lines changed for 2026 (2020 presidential results are not available on these lines). Litigation against the new map remains possible.

AK.note: Single district. General election uses ranked-choice voting unless the November 3, 2026 repeal initiative passes.

AR.note: Racial-gerrymander challenge rejected June 2025; HJR 1001 died.

CA.mapInUse2026: Proposition 50 map (approved November 4, 2025), in force through 2030
CA.note: Federal challenge failed (district court January 2026; Supreme Court denied February 4, 2026). 2020 results are not available on these lines.

CO.note: Colorado Supreme Court held mid-decade redistricting unconstitutional (June 29, 2026); a November 2026 ballot measure would ban it outright.

FL.mapInUse2026: HB 1D map signed May 4, 2026 (21 of 28 districts redrawn)
FL.note: Florida Supreme Court declined to block the map for 2026 (June 10, 2026); two Fair Districts suits are pending on the merits and could force a redraw for 2028. 2020 results are not available on these lines.

GA.note: Gov. Kemp's June 17, 2026 special session was called to redraw for 2028 after Callais; legislators declined to take up maps. A redraw in the 2027 regular session remains likely to be attempted. Senate and House generals have a majority/runoff rule (runoff December 5, 2028).

IL.note: Democratic leaders discussed a counter-redraw; no formal proposal.

IN.note: The Indiana Senate rejected a mid-decade map on December 11, 2025; five of the seven Republican senators who voted no lost renomination in May 2026, so a 2027 attempt is plausible.

KS.note: A 2026 special-session redraw stalled (about 20 votes short of a veto-proof majority); leadership has said it will try again.

LA.mapInUse2026: May 29, 2026 map adopted after Louisiana v. Callais struck the 2024 map
LA.note: New map is under challenge. Election rules: 2026 used a one-year open primary (Nov 3) with a Dec 12 runoff (HB 842); from 2028 congressional races use closed party primaries with a plurality general election (Act 1 of 2024). 2020 results are not available on these lines.

ME.note: Federal general elections use ranked-choice tabulation.

MD.note: Question 3 on the November 3, 2026 ballot would exempt congressional districts from the state constitution's compactness rules; if approved, a 2027 redraw aimed at 2028 is expected (dismantling MD-01).

MS.note: Gov. Reeves cancelled the May 20, 2026 special session; a redraw targeting MS-02 is expected to be attempted in 2027 for 2028.

MO.mapInUse2026: 2022 map, by order of the U.S. Supreme Court (September 25, 2026, 26A388) pending the referendum on the 2025 map
MO.note: Proposition A on the November 3, 2026 ballot decides whether the 2025 map (which splits Kansas City) takes effect; if approved, 2028 uses the 2025 map and MO-05 changes character. The inventory keys districts by number on the 2022 map.

NH.note: Gov. Ayotte declined a mid-decade redraw.

NJ.note: Gov. Sherrill open to a redraw after 2026; would need a constitutional referendum.

NY.note: A constitutional amendment allowing a mid-decade redraw passed first reading June 3, 2026; it needs second passage in 2027 and a November 2027 referendum to apply in 2028. The Supreme Court blocked a court-ordered NY-11 redraw on March 2, 2026.

NC.note: A three-judge panel allowed the map (November 26, 2025). 2020 results are not available on these lines.

OH.mapInUse2026: October 31, 2025 commission map (unanimous), in force through 2031
OH.note: 2020 results are not available on these lines.

SC.note: A May 2026 push to redraw SC-06 for 2026 failed in the state Senate; a 2027 attempt for 2028 is possible after Callais.

TN.note: A federal judge declined to block the map (May 26, 2026); ACLU litigation continues. 2020 results are not available on these lines.

TX.note: The Supreme Court stayed the November 2025 injunction (December 4, 2025) and reversed the district court in April 2026 (Abbott v. LULAC); merits litigation continues. 2020 results are not available on these lines.

UT.mapInUse2026: Court-ordered map (November 10, 2025) creating a Salt Lake City district under Proposition 4
UT.note: A Republican effort to repeal Proposition 4 failed to qualify (March 26, 2026); the legislature could adopt a new Prop-4-compliant map for 2028. 2020 results are not available on these lines.

VA.mapInUse2026: 2021 commission map (the April 21, 2026 referendum map was voided by the Supreme Court of Virginia on May 8, 2026)
VA.note: Democrats can restart the amendment process (passage in two sessions around the November 2027 House of Delegates election, then a referendum) — tight for 2028.

WA.mapInUse2026: 2022 commission map (as amended by court order 2024)
WA.note: A redraw needs a constitutional amendment; leadership calls 2028 unlikely.

WI.note: The Wisconsin Supreme Court heard a Democratic challenge to the congressional map in September 2026; a decision could order new lines for 2028.
